LESSON: VIRTUES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: AKHALAQ
Topic 5.1: Virtues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Virtues. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should a Muslim work?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam
2. explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah
3. describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings
4. appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VIRTUES
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Virtues helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: VIRTUES
Study Virtues like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: State the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam

What this means
In this part you learn to state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Virtues” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Virtues in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings

What this means
In this part you learn to describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Virtues” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Virtues is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Virtues” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Virtues in your own words. (skill: explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings)

Example 4: Show how “Virtues” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Virtues to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam.
3. Practise this skill: explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah.
4. Practise this skill: describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Virtues from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Virtues: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Virtues?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should a Muslim work?
2. Why is work considered an act of Ibadah?
3. What kind of work is prohibited in Islam?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Virtues means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam.
5. Be able to: explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
